name: Garlic Butter Beef Rice Bowl
pitch: Simple, savory, and deeply satisfying — this one-pan meal turns two humble ingredients into something the whole family will ask for again.
steps: Cook your rice according to package directions.
While rice cooks, heat a drizzle of oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Add ground beef and break it apart as it browns, about 6-8 minutes.
Drain excess fat if needed, then add 2-3 minced garlic cloves and a tablespoon of butter. Stir for 1-2 minutes until fragrant.
Season generously with salt, pepper, and a splash of soy sauce for depth.
Spoon the beef over rice and serve — feel free to add a fried egg on top if you have one!
toolSuggestion: A wide skillet or cast iron pan

name: DIY Beef Taco Rice Skillet
pitch: All the cozy flavors of taco night mixed into one skillet — no tortillas needed, and it comes together fast.
steps: Cook rice according to package directions.
Brown the ground beef in a skillet over medium-high heat, breaking it up as it cooks. Drain excess fat.
Season the beef with cumin, chili powder, garlic, salt, and pepper — about a teaspoon each of the spices, adjusted to your taste.
Stir the cooked rice right into the skillet with the beef and mix well so the spices coat everything.
Taste and adjust seasoning. This is simple but satisfying on its own, and even better with shredded cheese or salsa if you have them.
toolSuggestion: A large skillet with a lid

name: Asian-Style Beef Fried Rice
pitch: Soy sauce and a hot pan work magic here — this tastes like takeout and uses exactly what you have.
steps: Cook rice ahead of time and let it cool if you can — even 10 minutes helps it fry better and not go mushy. Day-old rice is ideal.
Heat a generous drizzle of oil in a large skillet or wok over high heat until it's very hot.
Add ground beef and cook, breaking it into small crumbles, until browned — about 5-6 minutes. Push it to the side.
Add the rice to the hot pan and let it sit undisturbed for 1-2 minutes to get a little crispy on the bottom.
Mix the beef and rice together, then add 2-3 tablespoons of soy sauce, a splash of rice or white vinegar, and minced garlic. Stir-fry everything together for 2-3 more minutes.
Taste and adjust with more soy sauce or a pinch of pepper. A drizzle of sesame oil would be amazing here if you have it!
toolSuggestion: A wok or the largest skillet you own
